eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus on Polymarket heavily favors a Tokyo daily maximum of 30–32°C on August 22, 2026, with 31°C (40%) leading, followed by 30°C (29.5%) and 32°C (23.5%).** Higher outcomes (33°C+) carry low implied probability, reflecting expectations that typical late-summer conditions will moderate the peak.

Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts issued August 21–22 project a maximum of 31–32°C (some models 33°C), with minimums near 24°C. This aligns closely with the climatological normal high of ~30.7°C for mid-to-late August. Hourly observations and short-range models show temperatures climbing toward 30–31°C by midday before afternoon cloud build-up and scattered showers or thunderstorms (precipitation probability rising to 50% in the 12–18 UTC window) limit further warming. High humidity (often 65–80%) and light-to-moderate easterly or southerly winds further suppress sensible heating.

Recent days provide context: August 21 reached ~32–33°C under partly cloudy skies, but increasing moisture and convective activity on the 22nd are expected to cap the peak. No strong heat dome, subsidence, or clear-sky anomaly is present to push readings into the mid-30s. The market’s tight clustering around 30–32°C therefore reflects the balance between seasonal warmth and the cooling influence of expected afternoon convection and cloud cover. New JMA updates or real-time observations through the afternoon will be the key near-term drivers.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Shanghai Pudong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Shanghai Pudong International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/shanghai/ZSPD.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and current observations position 30°C and 31°C as the leading outcomes for Shanghai’s highest temperature on August 22, 2026, aligning with the market’s 45% and 31% implied probabilities.**

Persistent cloud cover, scattered showers or thunderstorms, and elevated humidity (often 80–90%) have limited daytime solar heating and kept afternoon peaks moderated. Official and private forecasts from sources such as WeatherBug, Worldmeteo, and local meteorological updates consistently project a daily maximum of 30–31°C (86–88°F), with some hourly trends showing brief rises to around 30°C before precipitation or increased cloudiness suppresses further warming. This matches Shanghai’s late-August climatology, where average highs near 32°C are frequently tempered by monsoon-season moisture and convective activity.

Lower probabilities assigned to 29°C or 32°C+ reflect the narrow but plausible range of model outcomes: stronger rain timing could cap the high near 29°C, while any clearing could allow a brief push to 32°C. No extreme heat signals or unusual atmospheric patterns (such as a strong subtropical high) have emerged to shift consensus away from the 30–31°C band. Updated model runs and official briefings through the afternoon will provide the final data points most likely to influence remaining market movement before resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/my/sepang-district/WMKK.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from official and ensemble models indicate peak afternoon temperatures in Kuala Lumpur will likely reach 34–35°C under partly cloudy skies with scattered convection. High humidity near 50–70% during peak heating hours and light southerly winds will influence the exact maximum, as any earlier or more widespread thunderstorm activity could cap readings near 34°C while clearer intervals allow brief spikes to 35°C. These conditions align with the southwest monsoon pattern, where typical August highs average around 32–33°C but recent days have trended warmer. The near-even market split between 34°C and 35°C reflects model uncertainty in afternoon cloud timing and intensity ahead of the daily maximum window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and real-time observations position 33–35°C as the most probable range for Guangzhou’s official daily maximum on August 22, 2026.** Subtropical summer conditions under a strong western Pacific subtropical high typically support highs near the 1991–2020 climatological average of 33.2°C, while scattered thunderstorms and cloud cover—common during the East Asian monsoon—introduce variability that caps extreme heating yet allows brief clearing to push readings higher.

Current forecasts cluster tightly around 33–35.5°C, reflecting model consensus on modest instability and easterly flow that limits both extreme heat and rapid cooling. Historical records show 35.6°C as the all-time August 22 peak (2009), with recent years frequently reaching 34–35°C under similar patterns, lending weight to the market’s heavier weighting on those outcomes. Lower probabilities for 36°C+ or sub-32°C align with the low likelihood of exceptional clearing or persistent heavy rain on this date. Updated model runs and official station reports from the Guangzhou Meteorological Observatory will refine these odds as the afternoon peak approaches.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources including Météo-France, WeatherBug, and global numerical guidance (GFS) converge on a daytime maximum of 23–25 °C for Paris on 23 August 2026 under partly cloudy skies and a light northeast breeze.** 

This places the modal outcome squarely at 24 °C, aligning with the market’s strongest implied probability (54.5 %). Typical late-August climatology for the Paris region shows an average daily high near 24–25 °C; current conditions reflect a stable high-pressure regime with minimal warm-air advection or convective development, keeping temperatures close to seasonal norms rather than extremes. 

Recent model runs over the past 24–48 hours have shown little spread or trend, reinforcing trader consensus around the narrow 23–25 °C band (cumulative ~92 %). Resolution depends on the official Météo-France or equivalent station reading of the calendar-day maximum; any last-minute shift in cloud cover or wind would need to exceed ~2 °C to meaningfully alter the distribution.

Southwest flow, dew points around 24–25°C, and moderate humidity support peak readings in that narrow band, while residual moisture and variable timing of any remaining afternoon clouds introduce the main uncertainty between 30°C and 33°C outcomes. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent monsoon-driven cloud cover and rainfall are the dominant factors capping Lucknow's daytime maximum near 31–33°C on August 23, 2026.** Official India Meteorological Department (IMD) guidance issued August 21 forecasts a maximum of 33°C under overcast-to-generally-cloudy skies with scattered rain or thundershowers, consistent with active monsoon conditions across eastern Uttar Pradesh. Multiple private models align closely, projecting 31–32°C (WeatherBug ~31°C, Met Office 32°C) amid high humidity and widespread convective activity.

Recent excess rainfall (46% above normal in the preceding week) and a low-pressure system over northeast Madhya Pradesh have sustained moist, unstable air and extensive cloudiness, limiting solar heating and preventing the clearer-sky spikes that could push highs to 34°C or above. Historical August climatology for Lucknow centers on 32–33°C maxima, but the current pattern of frequent showers suppresses outliers. Market-implied odds therefore cluster tightly around the 31–33°C band, reflecting trader consensus that ongoing monsoon dynamics will hold the daily peak in this narrow, observationally supported range rather than allowing significant deviation. Updated IMD or NWP model runs on August 22–23 will be the next key data points for any probability shifts.
